Title: two Qs: Reinforcements and Clio's Kiss

Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
Reinforcements text: "Choose one or more Methuselahs.
Successful referendum means each chosen Methuselah selects
up to 3 library cards from his or her ash heap and shuffles
them into his or her library. Remove this card from the
game, even if the action is canceled or blocked or the
referendum fails."

I think this means that even if Reinforcements is canceled
by Direct Intervention (or Rewind Time), it's removed from
the game. Right?

What about Delaying Tactics? Presumably the card should
still be removed from the game, but what's the timing on
that? Is it removed from the game when played (ie it's
never in the ash heap at all, or goes immediately from ash
heap to out-of-game)? Or does it hang around until the
action resolves? Until the referendum resolves? If the
referendum is Delayed, does the acting Methuselah return
the Reinforcements to her hand, discard to hand size, and
then remove Reinforcements from the game, or is
Reinforcements already out-of-game and therefore Delay's
instruction to return it to hand "fizzles"?

Clio's Kiss text: "(D) Choose a vampire card another
Methuselah is contesting with you. That Methuselah yields
that copy. If there are no other Methuselah's contesting
the vampire, place your copy of the vampire face up in
your ={controlled}= region, untapped."

Cards being contested are not in play, and therefore can't
have actions directed at them, right? Is the (D) symbol
on this card telling us that Clio's Kiss is actually
directed at the Methuselah who's contesting the card with
you, or is it actually an undirected action (like Grasp
the Ghostly) and the (D) symbol was a mistake?

thanks,

Josh

hates getting kissed...

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Joshua Duffin wrote:
>
> Reinforcements text: "Choose one or more Methuselahs.
> Successful referendum means each chosen Methuselah selects
> up to 3 library cards from his or her ash heap and shuffles
> them into his or her library. Remove this card from the
> game, even if the action is canceled or blocked or the
> referendum fails."
>
> I think this means that even if Reinforcements is canceled
> by Direct Intervention (or Rewind Time), it's removed from
> the game. Right?

No. DI cancels the card play (before the action gets started).
Change of Target (e.g.) cancels the action.

When DI is played, all part of the canceled card's text are
ignored.

> What about Delaying Tactics? Presumably the card should
> still be removed from the game, but what's the timing on
> that? Is it removed from the game when played (ie it's
> never in the ash heap at all, or goes immediately from ash
> heap to out-of-game)? Or does it hang around until the
> action resolves? Until the referendum resolves? If the
> referendum is Delayed, does the acting Methuselah return
> the Reinforcements to her hand, discard to hand size, and
> then remove Reinforcements from the game, or is
> Reinforcements already out-of-game and therefore Delay's
> instruction to return it to hand "fizzles"?

It is out of the game, so cannot be affected by DT. DT will
cancel the referendum, but will fail to return the card from
out of play to the player's hand.

> Clio's Kiss text: "(D) Choose a vampire card another
> Methuselah is contesting with you. That Methuselah yields
> that copy. If there are no other Methuselah's contesting
> the vampire, place your copy of the vampire face up in
> your ={controlled}= region, untapped."
>
> Cards being contested are not in play, and therefore can't
> have actions directed at them, right? Is the (D) symbol

Unless card text says otherwise (like CK does), right.

> on this card telling us that Clio's Kiss is actually
> directed at the Methuselah who's contesting the card with
> you, or is it actually an undirected action (like Grasp
> the Ghostly) and the (D) symbol was a mistake?

The action is directed at the target out-of-play vampire and
thus at its controller (the Methuselah who is paying to contest
that copy - the Methuselah who would control it if all other
copies were yielded).

I thought the (D) symbol was currently considered reminder
text, and it's the target of an action that tells us whether
it's directed. Not so? Or do you mean that Clio's Kiss's
text allows it to target a contested card? (If so, that I
can understand, but not how that can make the action
directed - see below...)

> > on this card telling us that Clio's Kiss is actually
> > directed at the Methuselah who's contesting the card with
> > you, or is it actually an undirected action (like Grasp
> > the Ghostly) and the (D) symbol was a mistake?
>
> The action is directed at the target out-of-play vampire and
> thus at its controller (the Methuselah who is paying to contest
> that copy - the Methuselah who would control it if all other
> copies were yielded).

But I don't see how we can refer to a card's "controller"
when the card isn't actually controlled. How can Clio's
Kiss can be meaningfully directed at a card that's out of
play; doesn't "out of play" mean it's "not considered to
be in the play area" or something like that?

I'm not clear on how this differs from Grasp the Ghostly.
Grasp the Ghostly is undirected because the ash heap is
not "controlled". This seems to me a lot like Clio's Kiss,
since contested cards (vampires) are also not "controlled".
Unless the target is the Methuselah and not the card, it
doesn't make sense (to me) for Clio's Kiss to be directed -
and it seems clear that the target isn't the Methuselah but
the contested card. (If it were the Methuselah, it should
say something like: "Choose a Methuselah. That Methuselah
yields a vampire card of your choice that she is contesting
with you. [...]")

Josh

uncontrolled region are.

Thanks for the reference. I agree that it makes sense for
Darius, Lazar, and Clio's Kiss's effects to be blockable by
the person they're going to affect. But it seems to me that,
with the increase in effects affecting ash heaps (certainly
including one's own), your ash heap should probably be
likewise "defensible", counter to what you wrote in that
thread:

"The ash heap, on the other hand, is not a "resource" for the
player. The cards contained therein are not, in general, cards
that the player hopes to control. So the need to allow the
prey/predator to block the minion-gaining effect of Daemonic
Possession outweighs the need of the "target" to protect her
ash heap."

Either way, another thing I'd suggest would be good to have
spelled out in the rulebook, so people don't (like me) get
confused over what is and isn't "controlled enough" to
count as causing a directed action. :-)

Josh
